solution:
Both sides count ordered selections of distinct objects without repetition, so \({}^{n}P_{r} = \frac{n!}{(n-r)!}\).
\(\frac{{}^{n}P_{6}}{{}^{n}P_{3}} = \frac{n!/(n-6)!}{n!/(n-3)!} = \frac{(n-3)!}{(n-6)!} = (n-3)(n-4)(n-5)\).
So \((n-3)(n-4)(n-5) = 120 = 6 \times 5 \times 4\), and three consecutive decreasing factors force \(n-3 = 6\).
\(n = 9\)

\({}^{k}P_{2} = k(k-1)\), an ordered choice of 2 distinct objects from \(k\).
\((m+n)(m+n-1) = 56 = 8 \times 7\), so \(m+n = 8\).
\((m-n)(m-n-1) = 12 = 4 \times 3\), so \(m-n = 4\).
Adding, \(2m = 12\), and subtracting, \(2n = 4\).
\(m = 6,\ n = 2\)

Start from the right-hand side, using \({}^{(n+1)}P_{r} = \frac{(n+1)!}{(n+1-r)!}\).
RHS \(= (n-r+1) \times \frac{(n+1)!}{(n+1-r)!}\).
Since \((n+1-r)! = (n+1-r)(n-r)!\) and \(n+1-r = n-r+1\), the factor \((n-r+1)\) cancels:
RHS \(= \frac{(n+1)!}{(n-r)!} = (n+1) \times \frac{n!}{(n-r)!} = (n+1)\left({}^{n}P_{r}\right) = \) LHS.
Hence \((n+1)\left({}^{n}P_{r}\right) = (n-r+1)\left[{}^{(n+1)}P_{r}\right]\).

MADHURI has 7 letters, all different: M, A, D, H, U, R, I.
A 4-letter word is an ordered arrangement, and repetition is allowed, so each of the 4 places can be filled independently in 7 ways.
Number of words \(= 7^{4} = 2401\).
\(2401\)

The 7 letters of MADHURI are all different, and now no letter may repeat, so we make an ordered selection of 4 from 7.
Number of words \(= {}^{7}P_{4} = 7 \times 6 \times 5 \times 4 = 840\).
\(840\)

ALGORITHM has 9 different letters: vowels A, O, I (3) and consonants L, G, R, T, H, M (6).
Treat the 3 vowels as one block, so 6 consonants and 1 block, that is 7 units, are arranged in \(7! = 5040\) ways.
The 3 vowels inside the block are themselves arranged in \(3! = 6\) ways.
Number of arrangements \(= 5040 \times 6 = 30240\).
\(30240\)

First arrange the 6 distinct consonants of ALGORITHM in \(6! = 720\) ways.
This creates 7 gaps (5 between them and 2 at the ends); to keep no two vowels adjacent, the 3 distinct vowels must occupy 3 different gaps, which is an ordered choice: \({}^{7}P_{3} = 7 \times 6 \times 5 = 210\) ways.
Number of arrangements \(= 720 \times 210 = 151200\).
\(151200\)

There are 9 places, of which the even places are the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th, only 4 in number, while ALGORITHM has 6 consonants. So the condition means every even place is filled by a consonant, the vowels being confined to the odd places.
Choose and arrange 4 of the 6 distinct consonants in the 4 even places: \({}^{6}P_{4} = 6 \times 5 \times 4 \times 3 = 360\) ways.
The remaining 5 letters (2 consonants and 3 vowels), all distinct, fill the 5 odd places in \(5! = 120\) ways.
Number of arrangements \(= 360 \times 120 = 43200\).
\(43200\)

In ALGORITHM the first place is fixed as O and the last as T, so those two letters can be placed in only 1 way.
The remaining 7 letters are all different and fill the 7 middle places in \(7! = 5040\) ways.
\(5040\)

First row: the principal occupies the fixed middle seat, and the 6 distinct teachers fill the remaining 6 seats in \(6!\) ways.
Second row: arrange the 12 distinct boys first, in \(12!\) ways. They create 13 gaps (11 between them and 2 at the ends), and to keep no two girls together the 6 distinct girls must occupy 6 different gaps, an ordered choice: \({}^{13}P_{6} = \frac{13!}{7!}\).
Total \(= 6! \times 12! \times \frac{13!}{7!}\), and since \(\frac{6!}{7!} = \frac{1}{7}\) this simplifies.
Number of arrangements \(= \frac{12! \times 13!}{7}\)

HISTORY has 7 different letters.
Tie Y and T into one block, so 5 other letters and 1 block, that is 6 units, are arranged in \(6! = 720\) ways.
Within the block Y and T can stand in either order, \(2! = 2\) ways.
Number of arrangements \(= 720 \times 2 = 1440\).
\(1440\)

Here Y must immediately follow T, so the pair is the fixed block TY (unlike part (a), the order inside the block is not free).
The block together with the other 5 distinct letters gives 6 units, arranged in \(6! = 720\) ways.
\(720\)

All 7 letters of HISTORY are different and every one is used, so this is a plain arrangement of 7 distinct objects.
Number of arrangements \(= 7! = 5040\).
\(5040\)

The vowels of HISTORY are I and O. They must take the first and the last place, in \(2! = 2\) ways.
The remaining 5 distinct letters fill the 5 middle places in \(5! = 120\) ways.
Number of arrangements \(= 2 \times 120 = 240\).
\(240\)

The last two places are fixed as S and T in that order, so they contribute 1 way.
The remaining 5 distinct letters fill the first 5 places in \(5! = 120\) ways.
\(120\)

S is fixed in the first place and T in the last place, in 1 way.
The remaining 5 distinct letters fill the 5 middle places in \(5! = 120\) ways.
\(120\)

SOLAPUR has 7 different letters: 4 consonants S, L, P, R and 3 vowels O, A, U.
With 4 consonants and 3 vowels in 7 places, the only alternating pattern is C V C V C V C, so the consonants take the odd places and the vowels the even places; there is just 1 such pattern.
Consonants arrange in \(4! = 24\) ways and vowels in \(3! = 6\) ways.
Number of arrangements \(= 24 \times 6 = 144\).
\(144\)

There are 6 available digits 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8 and none is 0, so every arrangement is a genuine 4-digit number.
Repetition is allowed, so each of the 4 places is filled independently in 6 ways.
Number of numbers \(= 6^{4} = 1296\).
\(1296\)

The 6 digits are distinct and none is 0, and now no digit may repeat, so we make an ordered selection of 4 from 6.
Number of numbers \(= {}^{6}P_{4} = 6 \times 5 \times 4 \times 3 = 360\).
\(360\)

A number between 100 and 1000 has exactly 3 digits, and repetition is not allowed.
The hundreds place cannot be 0, so it can be filled by any of 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, that is 5 ways.
The remaining two places are filled by an ordered choice of 2 from the 5 digits left (0 now being allowed): \({}^{5}P_{2} = 5 \times 4 = 20\) ways.
Number of numbers \(= 5 \times 20 = 100\).
\(100\)

The 6 digits 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 are distinct and all are used, so there are \(6! = 720\) such 6-digit numbers in all.
A number is divisible by 5 only if its units digit is 5 (there is no 0 available), which fixes 1 digit.
The other 5 distinct digits fill the remaining 5 places in \(5! = 120\) ways.
\(120\)

The total number of 6-digit numbers formed from 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 without repetition is \(6! = 720\), and 120 of them are divisible by 5 (those ending in 5).
Numbers not divisible by 5 \(= 720 - 120 = 600\).
\(600\)

The two letters are different and their order matters: \({}^{26}P_{2} = 26 \times 25 = 650\) ways.
The two digits are distinct and non-zero, so chosen in order from 1 to 9: \({}^{9}P_{2} = 9 \times 8 = 72\) ways.
Total code words \(= 650 \times 72 = 46800\).
For a code word ending in an even digit, the last digit is one of 2, 4, 6, 8, that is 4 ways, and the other digit is any of the 8 remaining non-zero digits, so the digit pair can be formed in \(4 \times 8 = 32\) ways, giving \(650 \times 32 = 20800\).
\(46800\) code words in all, of which \(20800\) end with an even digit.

The 5 letters are distinct and each one is posted independently; a box may receive any number of letters, so choices repeat freely.
Each letter can go into any of the 3 boxes, so there are 3 ways per letter.
Number of ways \(= 3^{5} = 243\).
\(243\)

We arrange 4 of 11 distinct objects in a row, and the specified object must be one of the 4.
It can occupy any one of the 4 places, in 4 ways.
The other 3 places are filled by an ordered choice of 3 from the remaining 10 objects: \({}^{10}P_{3} = 10 \times 9 \times 8 = 720\) ways.
Number of arrangements \(= 4 \times 720 = 2880\).
\(2880\)

If the specified object never occurs, all 4 places must be filled from the other 10 distinct objects, in order and without repetition.
Number of arrangements \(= {}^{10}P_{4} = 10 \times 9 \times 8 \times 7 = 5040\).
\(5040\)

The 5 books are all different and every one is placed, so this is an arrangement of 5 distinct objects in a row.
Number of ways \(= 5! = 120\).
\(120\)

Tie the 2 specified books into one block, so the block together with the other 3 books gives 4 units, arranged in \(4! = 24\) ways.
The 2 books inside the block can be interchanged in \(2! = 2\) ways.
Number of ways \(= 24 \times 2 = 48\).
\(48\)

Total arrangements of the 5 distinct books \(= 5! = 120\), and those in which the 2 specified books are together \(= 4! \times 2! = 48\).
Number with the 2 books never together \(= 120 - 48 = 72\).
\(72\)

The 3 boys and 3 girls are 6 distinct persons seated in a row with no condition.
Number of ways \(= 6! = 720\).
\(720\)

The two end seats must be taken by 2 of the 3 distinct girls, and the two ends are different seats, so this is an ordered choice: \({}^{3}P_{2} = 3 \times 2 = 6\) ways.
The remaining 4 persons (3 boys and 1 girl) fill the 4 middle seats in \(4! = 24\) ways.
Number of ways \(= 6 \times 24 = 144\).
\(144\)

With 3 boys and 3 girls in 6 seats, alternate seating admits only two patterns, B G B G B G and G B G B G B.
In each pattern the 3 distinct boys are arranged among their 3 seats in \(3! = 6\) ways and the 3 distinct girls among theirs in \(3! = 6\) ways.
Number of ways \(= 2 \times 3! \times 3! = 2 \times 6 \times 6 = 72\).
\(72\)
_note: The book's key gives 288 for this sub-item, which is 4 times the correct value. With equal numbers of boys and girls only two alternating patterns exist (BGBGBG and GBGBGB), so the count is \(2 \times 3! \times 3! = 72\); an exhaustive check of all 720 seatings confirms exactly 72 are alternating. The other three sub-items of Q17 (720, 144, 144) all reconcile with the key exactly, which marks (iii) as an isolated slip.

solution:
Tie the 3 boys into one block, so the block together with the 3 girls gives 4 units, arranged in \(4! = 24\) ways.
The 3 distinct boys inside the block are arranged in \(3! = 6\) ways.
Number of ways \(= 24 \times 6 = 144\).
\(144\)
